text: In validation error messages, use "Unrecognised" for values or IDs that are unexpected or absent from the expected source, and reserve "Invalid" for data that is malformed or structurally incorrect.
reason: This preserves the semantic distinction between unknown-but-well-formed values and genuinely invalid data, making validation feedback more accurate.
common_pattern: Terminology choice for validation errors: distinguish between well-formed values that are simply absent/unexpected in the source ('Unrecognised') and malformed or structurally incorrect data ('Invalid').

text: In Django querysets, use `.get()` when a filter is expected to match exactly one row based on a data invariant; use `.first()` only when multiple matches are possible or expected, and add an inline comment explaining why `.first()` is used instead of `.get()`.
reason: `.get()` raises `DoesNotExist` or `MultipleObjectsReturned` when uniqueness assumptions are violated, preventing silent selection of an arbitrary row. When `.first()` is intentional, documentation helps future maintainers understand why non-unique behavior is acceptable.
common_pattern: Choosing between Django queryset `.get()` and `.first()` based on expected cardinality, with explicit documentation when `.first()` is intentionally used for non-unique lookups.

text: PO import commands must not fall back to `entry.msgid` when `entry.msgstr` is empty; missing translations should remain untranslated rather than being stored as translated text.
reason: Substituting the source string for an empty translation pollutes the translated content and misrepresents translation state. Required-field or validation constraints should be handled separately, not by copying source text into translations.
common_pattern: Both sub-groups concern Wagtail localization translation import/export correctness, but they address different concerns: (a) docstrings accurately describing import/export direction and content, and (b) the PO import command not fabricating translations by substituting source text for empty msgstr.

text: When a variable is assigned only inside conditional branches or a try/except block and is referenced afterward, ensure every path binds it: initialize it to a default value before the block, provide an exhaustive else branch, or set a fallback value such as None in the exception handler.
reason: Prevents UnboundLocalError/NameError when input types or structures do not match expected cases, and makes defensive fallback behavior explicit.
common_pattern: Ensure that variables conditionally assigned inside if/try blocks are always bound on every path before being referenced after the block, preventing UnboundLocalError/NameError.

text: For DeepL FORMALITY, accept only 'default', 'prefer_less', and 'prefer_more' (the values that work across all locales), and raise a ValueError for any unsupported value instead of silently ignoring it.
reason: Both generalizations specify the same allowed value set based on DeepL cross-locale compatibility; the second adds the complementary requirement that invalid values fail loudly, so the two are merged into one complete validation rule.
common_pattern: Validation of DeepL FORMALITY parameter: only 'default', 'prefer_less', and 'prefer_more' are cross-locale compatible, and unsupported values must be rejected rather than silently ignored.

text: In wagtail_localize/strings.py inline tag validation/extraction, scan all inline tags with attributes — including custom inline tags — rather than only anchor (`<a>`) tags. Any inline tag with attributes is normalized by assigning an `id`, so do not reject HTML attributes merely because they are not `id` on `<a>`; such validation is redundant and can reject valid custom inline tags. Phrase any resulting error generically (e.g. `Unrecognised id: {}`) instead of hard-coding a specific tag name like `<a>`.
reason: `id` attributes are valid on any element, and the system already normalizes inline tags with attributes, so restricting extraction/validation to `<a>`/`id` omits legitimate cases, rejects valid custom inline tags, and yields misleading error messages.
common_pattern: Inline-tag validation in wagtail_localize should reflect its actual scope: validation function names should match broadened responsibility, and validation should not reject inputs that the system already normalizes.

text: Confirmation dialogs for destructive or content-overwriting admin actions must state the concrete consequence of proceeding and name the affected object, including distinguishing attributes such as source page title and locale (e.g., 'This will overwrite the contents of this page with the contents of {source_page.title} ({locale})'), instead of using a generic 'Are you sure?' prompt.
reason: Users cannot make an informed decision without knowing exactly what will be overwritten or destroyed and which specific object is involved, especially when multiple pages share the same title across locales.
common_pattern: Confirmation dialogs for destructive admin actions should be specific and informative, stating the concrete consequence and identifying the affected object rather than using a generic 'Are you sure?' prompt.

text: Use `gettext_lazy` for user-facing strings that are evaluated at import/class-definition time, attached to cached hooks or filters, or otherwise reused across requests/users (e.g. filter labels, `null_label`, `empty_label`, choice labels). Use `gettext`/`_()` for strings evaluated per request.
reason: Cached or class-level strings are reused across users, so eager translation can freeze them in the wrong locale. `gettext_lazy` defers translation until render/use time.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail gettext/i18n conventions: avoid shadowing the `_` translation alias, choose `gettext_lazy` vs eager `gettext` based on evaluation/caching lifetime, and format translatable strings for translators.

text: When querying Wagtail pages through `Page.objects`, append `.specific` if downstream logic depends on page-type-specific fields, methods, overrides, logging, alias conversion, or translations; omit `.specific` when the instance is used only for base `Page` behavior such as `get_children()`. Apply this choice consistently to related page lookups in the same flow.
reason: Base `Page` instances do not carry subclass-specific behavior, so `.specific` is required for concrete page-type logic. Conversely, `.specific` adds an unnecessary upcast/query overhead when only base-model behavior is used.
common_pattern: Wagtail `Page` retrieval should use `.specific` only when concrete page-type behavior/fields are required, and should avoid `.specific` when only base `Page` behavior is needed.

text: When recursively traversing or rebuilding StreamField paths in `wagtail_localize/models.py`, preserve the full remaining component list rather than truncating to a fixed depth, and keep content paths distinct from field paths: content paths identify paths within an instance (StreamBlock components are block IDs), while field paths identify paths on the data model (StreamBlock components are block type names). Do not assign field-path components to a content-path variable, especially when recursing into nested StreamBlocks.
reason: Fixed-depth truncation drops inner path segments for deeply nested blocks, and mixing content-path and field-path representations produces incorrect lookups when StreamBlocks are nested.
scope: file:wagtail_localize/models.py; project-specific Wagtail Localize StreamField path handling
common_pattern: Correct recursive StreamField path handling in `wagtail_localize/models.py`: preserve the complete remaining path components and keep content-path vs field-path representations distinct when walking nested StreamBlocks.

text: In Django, a post_save receiver that only cares about a specific field (e.g., activation/deactivation) must verify that the field actually changed before emitting signals or running logic — by capturing the previous value in a paired pre_save handler, checking update_fields, or persisting the last signalled state — rather than firing on every save of the model.
reason: Firing signals or logic unconditionally on post_save causes false activations and wasted work on unrelated saves. Explicit change detection keeps the handler scoped to the event it actually represents.
common_pattern: Prevent Django post_save handlers from firing on unrelated saves by explicitly detecting whether the relevant field actually changed before emitting signals or running logic.

text: In class-based admin views, do not add a `next` query parameter to action links when the destination view computes its own contextual success URL. An unnecessary `next` override can mask the view's default/contextual redirect logic and make the intended redirect unreachable. If a `next` override is required, keep it separate from default success URL computation (e.g., pass contextual redirect data to `get_default_success_url(object)`) and reserve `get_success_url()` for explicit `next` overrides.
reason: Prevents silent or inconsistent redirects in admin actions by ensuring contextual success URLs are not bypassed by a generic `next` parameter, while preserving explicit `next` routing where actually needed.
scope: class-based admin views (e.g., Wagtail admin hooks) in this codebase
common_pattern: Managing the `next` query parameter in admin action links/views to prevent it from masking context-sensitive success URL logic; avoid unnecessary `next` overrides when the view can determine the redirect itself, and keep contextual redirect data in the default success URL computation rather than relying on fallback behavior when `next` is present.

text: Management commands that mutate or seed data should be idempotent: use get_or_create/update_or_create (or equivalent create-if-missing logic) for required objects so reruns repair missing state, and emit output only when the command actually changes state (e.g., inactive -> active).
reason: Both comments describe expected behavior for Django management commands: one requires idempotent creation/update of required objects, the other requires output to reflect actual transitions. Together they form one principle for reliable, rerunnable commands.
common_pattern: Management commands that mutate or seed data should be idempotent and should only report actual state changes.

text: Keep shared 'apply' operation helpers single-purpose: they should accept only explicit dependencies (e.g. translation_id, user, translator) and perform only the core mutation, without reading request context or embedding validation, permission, or side-effect logic. Perform all precondition/permission checks at each entry point (view and form __init__/validation); when the same checks apply to multiple entry points, replicate them explicitly at each rather than centralizing them in the shared helper.
reason: A helper that mixes validation with mutation behaves unpredictably when reused from multiple call sites (views and forms), causing unintended consequences and hidden, duplicated validation. Keeping the helper pure and pushing guards to the boundaries keeps each unit testable, makes each caller's requirements explicit, and avoids coupling shared logic to any single caller's validation needs.
common_pattern: Separation of concerns between shared 'apply' operation helpers and their callers: helpers should be single-purpose, accept explicit dependencies, and perform only the core action; all validation/permission/precondition checks belong at each entry point (view and form init/validation), duplicated explicitly rather than centralized in the helper.

text: In `wagtail_localize/views/edit_translation.py`, when adding or updating widget mapping support for a chooser/block type in `widget_from_block()`, also update `widget_from_field()` to handle direct ForeignKey fields targeting the same model/class (e.g., media ForeignKey fields should map to `media_chooser`), so block and field representations resolve to consistent widget types.
reason: Translation editing UI consistency: a relationship can appear either as a block or as a direct ForeignKey field. Missing one path causes incorrect or missing widget rendering depending on how the field is declared.
common_pattern: Paired widget-mapping functions must be kept in sync so equivalent block and direct ForeignKey representations resolve to the same widget type.

text: In sync/update methods that accumulate changes behind a single `should_save` dirty flag before calling `.save()` once, every branch that mutates a scalar instance field must set `should_save = True`. Note that M2M/relationship changes applied via manager methods (e.g., `.set()`, `.add()`) persist immediately and do not require the flag — so distinguish scalar fields (flag + save) from relation assignments (direct manager call).
reason: A forgotten flag assignment silently discards an in-memory change because the final `.save()` is skipped. Conversely, gating M2M manager calls behind the flag is misleading because they persist independently.
scope: sync/update methods using a `should_save` accumulator flag
common_pattern: Dirty-flag (`should_save`) synchronization: mutating branches in a field-by-field sync method must set the flag so a single guarded `.save()` persists all changes, with careful handling of fields (like M2M) that persist independently.

text: Keep language-code handling logic (e.g., `language_code()` methods) local to each machine translator backend in `wagtail_localize/machine_translators/` rather than consolidating it into a shared utility, because each backend has its own special cases for interpreting and formatting locale codes.
reason: Different translation backends have backend-specific quirks in how they interpret/format language codes; a unified implementation would either be incorrect for some backends or accumulate backend-specific branching.
common_pattern: Design and testing conventions for the per-backend `language_code()` normalization logic in `wagtail_localize/machine_translators/`. The cluster contains two related sub-patterns: (1) where that logic should live, and (2) how its normalization behavior must be tested. Note that Generalizations 1 and 2 form a resolved contradiction within PR#125 (a merge suggestion was overruled in favor of backend-local implementations).

text: Form fields that depend on an optional integration (e.g., machine translation) must be added or removed in the form's `__init__` based on runtime configuration, using the same integration-availability helper used elsewhere — not conditionally hidden in the template.
reason: Keeps conditional field-presence logic in the form definition instead of template workarounds, aligns the form UI with actually configured capabilities, and makes the conditional behavior easier to test without exposing unusable options to users.
common_pattern: Conditionally exposing form fields/controls based on whether an optional integration is configured — the implementation should gate field presence in the form definition (not the template), and both states (available/unavailable) must be tested.

text: In test model definitions (e.g. `wagtail_localize/test/models.py`), include only the fields, `translatable_fields`, and `panels` required by the behavior under test, and only use Wagtail snippet machinery (`@register_snippet`, `ClusterableModel`) when the test specifically needs snippet admin behavior; otherwise define a plain `TranslatableMixin` model.
reason: Snippet registration adds admin/modeladmin behavior unrelated to most tests (e.g. verifying drafts cannot be saved), inflating complexity and obscuring the behavior actually under test. Minimal, non-snippet test models keep tests focused and reduce incidental coupling.
common_pattern: Testing discipline: both sub-patterns concern writing focused, purpose-driven tests — either by keeping the test *fixtures/models* minimal and free of irrelevant framework machinery, or by asserting the *invariants* that define correct copy/translation behavior rather than a single superficial field. The common thread is 'make the test exercise exactly the behavior under test and prove it fully', but the two generalizations target different artifacts (test model definitions vs. test assertions).

text: Tests for model copy/translation operations should assert the copy's target `locale`, its `translation_key` relationship to the source, and that the returned object is a distinct instance from the source — not just a copied scalar field such as `title`.
reason: A copy/translation method must create a new localized record while preserving the translation linkage. Without these assertions, bugs where the source is returned, mutated, or given the wrong locale can pass silently.
common_pattern: Testing discipline: both sub-patterns concern writing focused, purpose-driven tests — either by keeping the test *fixtures/models* minimal and free of irrelevant framework machinery, or by asserting the *invariants* that define correct copy/translation behavior rather than a single superficial field. The common thread is 'make the test exercise exactly the behavior under test and prove it fully', but the two generalizations target different artifacts (test model definitions vs. test assertions).

text: In machine translator tests, mock the external HTTP POST (e.g. `requests.post`) rather than making live API calls or mocking the translator's `translate()` method. Then assert the public `translate()` behavior: it selects the correct endpoint based on the auth key, returns a dict mapping each source string to `StringValue(translated_text)` on success, and raises for error HTTP statuses.
reason: Mocking the HTTP boundary keeps tests deterministic, fast, and independent of network access, credentials, rate limits, and third-party availability, while still exercising the translator's request construction and response parsing. Mocking `translate()` bypasses the code under test; live calls introduce flakiness and unwanted external side effects.
scope: machine translator / provider integration tests, e.g. wagtail_localize/machine_translators/tests/
common_pattern: Deterministic testing of machine translator integrations by mocking the external HTTP boundary and asserting the public `translate()` behavior, instead of making live API calls, mocking `translate()` itself, or only testing internal helpers.

text: In Django/Wagtail test helper/factory functions, make the helper the single source of model setup: create persisted instances with `model.objects.create(**kwargs)`, name parameters that accept a model instance `instance` or `object` (not `model`), and have callers rely on the helper instead of duplicating dependent model state in `setUp` or test bodies.
reason: Reduces test boilerplate, avoids duplicated or missed setup, and prevents ambiguity between model classes and model instances.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail test helper and factory functions should encapsulate model creation and preparation, use idiomatic manager-based creation and unambiguous instance parameter names, and callers should rely on the helper rather than duplicating its setup.

text: Keep test code focused and consistent: scope fixtures, mocks, and helpers to the tests that need them, and use one consistent request/helper API across the test class while preserving existing shared helpers that already have multiple call sites.
reason: Prevents unrelated fixture semantics and shared setup from implying behavior the test does not verify, while avoiding inconsistent request abstractions and unnecessary replacement of established helpers.
common_pattern: Test code should minimize incidental setup and use consistent helper abstractions, keeping fixtures, mocks, and helpers scoped to the behavior under test.

text: Before writing a new test for multi-locale translation submission redirect behavior, check whether existing multi-locale submission tests already cover the scenario; only add a test if it is not already covered. When added, the test should submit a translation to 2+ locales and assert the user is redirected back to the previous location.
reason: Avoids redundant test coverage while ensuring multi-locale submission redirects are guarded against regressions.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern test coverage for multi-locale translation submission redirect behavior: one proposes adding such a test, the other cautions that existing tests may already cover it. Together they form a complementary pair — write the test only if not already covered.

text: Test comments must accurately describe the method under test's actual behavior and return semantics, and must agree with the assertion. If a comment describes an unrelated method such as `__str__` or contradicts the assertion, update the comment or the implementation so they agree.
reason: Diverging test comments and assertions mislead future readers about intended behavior and may signal a broken test or documentation bug.
common_pattern: Test comments must accurately describe the actual behavior and return semantics of the method under test and remain consistent with the assertion; they must not describe unrelated methods or contradict observed behavior.

text: Do not create test utility helpers that only delegate to Django's `reverse()`; call `reverse()` directly at the test call site, and remove any existing pass-through (including version-compatibility) wrappers by inlining them.
reason: Pass-through helpers add unnecessary indirection, keep tests less explicit about URL resolution, and preserve obsolete compatibility layers that accumulate over time.
common_pattern: Both generalizations state the same principle from two angles: remove (Generalization 1) and do-not-add (Generalization 2) test helpers that only delegate to Django's `reverse()`. This is an inverse pair (removal vs. prohibition) of a single rule about avoiding pass-through helpers around `reverse()` in tests.

text: In translation publishing tests, mirror the Snippet publish/draft tests against the equivalent Page tests (both go through Translation.save_target()), and assert the logged revision equals the object's live_revision (e.g., assertEqual(log.revision, obj.live_revision)) rather than only asserting that TranslationLog.page_revision is a Revision instance.
reason: Both Pages and Snippets publish via Translation.save_target(), so they need equivalent regression coverage, and the page_revision FK now targets a generic Revision; comparing the logged revision to live_revision proves both that the log record is correct and that publishing actually set the live revision.
common_pattern: Tests covering translation publishing workflows (Pages and Snippets) via Translation.save_target() should verify the revision recorded in TranslationLog, and the strongest verification is comparing the logged revision to the object's live_revision rather than merely checking the type.

text: In Django tests, explicitly manage `transaction.on_commit` callbacks: patch or mock `on_commit` only within the specific tests that require controlled execution (not in shared `setUp`), and execute or capture callbacks before asserting on deferred/committed state such as `live_revision`.
reason: Django's `TestCase` does not automatically run `on_commit` callbacks, so deferred side effects may not have executed when assertions run. Additionally, patching `on_commit` around shared `setUp` unnecessarily affects unrelated tests and obscures intent.
common_pattern: Correct handling of Django's `transaction.on_commit` deferred callbacks in tests: scope patching narrowly and ensure callbacks execute before assertions on committed state.

text: When testing against multiple versions of an external service such as a database in tox, define separate version-specific tox environments named after the service and version (e.g., postgres12, postgres15), pin a client driver version compatible with that server version, and ensure each environment provisions the actual service/container and passes the required connection environment variables; adding only the client dependency does not run tests against that service.
reason: Makes tested server/driver combinations explicit, avoids incompatible driver/server pairings, and prevents false confidence from tests silently using a default backend like SQLite.
common_pattern: Best practices for tox test environments that target multiple versions of an external service (e.g., PostgreSQL): define version-specific environments, pin a compatible client driver, and actually provision the service with connection environment variables so tests run against it.

text: For dirty-flag save patterns, write tests that mutate one field at a time (e.g., groups-only, password-only) so that branches forgetting to set `should_save = True` are caught.
reason: Each independently-mutable field corresponds to its own branch; testing them individually prevents a forgotten flag from going unnoticed.
scope: tests covering sync/update methods with a `should_save` flag
common_pattern: Dirty-flag (`should_save`) synchronization: mutating branches in a field-by-field sync method must set the flag so a single guarded `.save()` persists all changes, with careful handling of fields (like M2M) that persist independently.

text: For each machine translator implementation in `wagtail_localize/machine_translators/`, add a dedicated `test_language_code` in its corresponding `test_{translator}_translator.py` that verifies `language_code()` normalization: full locale codes (e.g., 'fr-fr') reduce to the base language subtag, and multi-segment codes (e.g., 'foo-bar-baz') fall back to the first segment. Use region-specific locale fixtures (e.g., 'fr-fr') rather than bare codes (e.g., 'fr') so the code path is actually exercised.
reason: The `language_code()` method is part of the translator interface; tests with bare language codes can pass trivially without exercising normalization, allowing regressions in locale mapping to the translation backend.
common_pattern: Design and testing conventions for the per-backend `language_code()` normalization logic in `wagtail_localize/machine_translators/`. The cluster contains two related sub-patterns: (1) where that logic should live, and (2) how its normalization behavior must be tested. Note that Generalizations 1 and 2 form a resolved contradiction within PR#125 (a merge suggestion was overruled in favor of backend-local implementations).

text: For form fields conditionally rendered based on an optional integration or external configuration, add tests for both states: field absent when the integration is unavailable, and field present when it is available.
reason: Ensures both branches of the conditional form behavior are verified, preventing regressions where unusable controls appear or required controls disappear.
common_pattern: Conditionally exposing form fields/controls based on whether an optional integration is configured — the implementation should gate field presence in the form definition (not the template), and both states (available/unavailable) must be tested.

text: When a Wagtail Localize setting changes a default behavior rather than disabling a capability, expose it as a mode-selection/default setting (e.g. `DEFAULT_<FEATURE>_MODE = 'mode-a' | 'mode-b'`) instead of a boolean `DISABLE_<FEATURE>` flag. A `DISABLE_*` name misrepresents behavior when the feature is still available and users can choose other modes.
reason: A `DISABLE_*` name misrepresents behavior when the feature is still available and users can choose other modes.
common_pattern: Wagtail Localize Django settings should be named and designed around actual behavior: prefer mode/default selection over misleading disable flags, use the consistent WAGTAILLOCALIZE_ namespace with concise behavior-based names, and handle optional settings backward-compatibly with explicit branching.

text: Read optional `WAGTAILLOCALIZE_*` behavior toggles with `getattr(settings, ..., default)` to preserve the existing default, but make the resulting behavior branch explicit (e.g. with if/else) rather than hiding the alternative in the `getattr` default.
reason: Keeps the package usable without explicit configuration and backward-compatible, while keeping toggled behavior clear and modifiable.
common_pattern: Wagtail Localize Django settings should be named and designed around actual behavior: prefer mode/default selection over misleading disable flags, use the consistent WAGTAILLOCALIZE_ namespace with concise behavior-based names, and handle optional settings backward-compatibly with explicit branching.

text: Do not hardcode the Wagtail admin URL prefix (e.g. `/admin/`) in frontend JS/TS code. Instead, inject the configured admin base URL from Django using `{% url 'wagtailadmin_home' %}` (for example as `window.adminUrl`) or receive it from the backend/props, and prepend it when constructing admin links or API paths.
reason: Wagtail can be mounted at a custom admin path such as `/cms/`, so hardcoded `/admin/` URLs break deployments that do not use the default admin URL.
common_pattern: Frontend code must not hardcode the Wagtail admin base path; it should derive or inject the configured admin URL from Django/Wagtail.

text: In setup.cfg, keep isort's `line_length` equal to flake8's `max-line-length` so import sorting and linting agree on the maximum allowed line length.
reason: Mismatched line lengths cause isort to wrap imports at a different width than flake8 permits, producing inconsistent formatting and avoidable churn.
common_pattern: setup.cfg tool configuration should be accurate and internally consistent—specifically, isort's line length must match flake8's, and isort's first-party classification must reference only the project's own package while letting external frameworks remain third-party.

text: In setup.cfg `[isort]`, configure `known_first_party` to the project's actual package name only; do not add custom `known_django` / `known_wagtail` sections—external frameworks should be classified as `THIRDPARTY` by default.
reason: Accurate first-party classification ensures the project's own imports are sorted correctly and avoids unnecessary custom sections for external dependencies.
common_pattern: setup.cfg tool configuration should be accurate and internally consistent—specifically, isort's line length must match flake8's, and isort's first-party classification must reference only the project's own package while letting external frameworks remain third-party.

text: Keep each tool's `rev` in `.pre-commit-config.yaml` pinned to the current latest upstream release, and keep it synchronized with the version referenced in the corresponding CI workflow (e.g. `.github/workflows/ruff.yml`).
reason: Using the latest release gets the newest fixes and avoids re-pinning soon after; syncing with CI avoids running different lint versions in local hooks vs. CI.
common_pattern: Managing linting/formatting tooling through pre-commit as the single source of truth — centralizing dependency versions there, running hooks locally before submission, and keeping hook revisions current and synchronized with CI.

text: Configure linter/formatter and packaging/sdist exclude lists minimally and maintainably: only exclude paths that can contain relevant files, and use glob patterns for repeated directory categories (e.g., `**/tests`) instead of enumerating each individual path.
reason: The cluster contains two convergent generalizations about replacing enumerated test directories with globs, plus a complementary generalization about dropping irrelevant exclusions such as `node_modules` or `.github` from linter configs. Together they define the same underlying principle for config exclusion lists: avoid dead entries and avoid brittle manual enumeration.
common_pattern: Configuration exclusion-list hygiene: keep exclude/skip lists minimal by removing paths that cannot contain relevant source files, and keep them maintainable by using glob patterns for repeated directory categories instead of enumerating every individual path.

text: For user-supplied configuration options with a restricted set of valid values, do not raise a hard error on invalid input; instead emit a warning and ignore the option or fall back to the default so the integration keeps working.
reason: Configuration mistakes should not be fatal. Tolerating them (with a warning) keeps integrations operational while still surfacing the problem to the operator. This is the option accepted in the PR discussion after the alternative of raising ValueError was considered and rejected.
common_pattern: Handling user-supplied configuration options that have a restricted set of valid values — specifically how to react to unsupported/invalid values (hard error vs. warn-and-fallback). The two generalizations are direct alternatives raised in the same review discussion.

text: When wrapping a third-party provider option whose accepted values vary by locale, restrict configuration to the subset supported across all target locales and document that cross-locale subset.
reason: Prevents users from selecting provider values that work only in some locales and fail silently or behave inconsistently elsewhere.
scope: provider integration options, especially machine translation formality/documentation
common_pattern: Third-party provider options that vary by locale should be constrained to the subset supported across all target locales, and that supported subset should be documented for users.

text: Maintain a minimal, valid, and readable `tox.ini` `envlist`: split large envlists across multiple lines and group them logically by compatible version-family factors; include all supported dependency versions up to the development-branch alias; use brace expansion to consolidate compatible factor combinations; omit incompatible or redundant version combinations; run reduced representative subsets for secondary backends such as sqlite; and remove superseded or dropped versions from every relevant section, including `envlist` and `deps`, rather than leaving both old and new matrices in place.
reason: A well-organized and accurate tox envlist makes valid/unsupported combinations easier to spot, keeps the CI/test matrix manageable, avoids invalid or redundant environments, and prevents dropped versions from lingering in mismatched tox sections.
common_pattern: Maintaining a consistent, valid, minimal tox/CI test matrix in tox.ini: envlist factor naming, basepython mappings, supported version combinations, dependency declarations, and keeping related config sections in sync.

text: In `tox.ini` and the CI build matrix, use tox-recognized factor names (e.g., `py{3.10}`, `main`, `django4.2`) rather than raw dependency specifiers or non-standard concatenated forms; when using custom or dotted Python factors, add/update explicit `basepython` mappings so each generated environment resolves to the correct interpreter.
reason: Tox maps factors to environments and interpreters; invalid or non-standard factor names can produce broken CI environments or prevent the intended Python version from being used.
common_pattern: Maintaining a consistent, valid, minimal tox/CI test matrix in tox.ini: envlist factor naming, basepython mappings, supported version combinations, dependency declarations, and keeping related config sections in sync.

text: Treat `.pre-commit-config.yaml` as the single source of truth for linting/formatting tool dependencies. Do not duplicate those lint dependencies (e.g. in `package.json`); instead add any lint tooling used in CI to the pre-commit config so local hooks and CI share the same rules and versions.
reason: Prevents duplicate version management and drift between pre-commit hook versions and package manager or CI tool versions, keeping local and CI linting aligned.
common_pattern: Managing linting/formatting tooling through pre-commit as the single source of truth — centralizing dependency versions there, running hooks locally before submission, and keeping hook revisions current and synchronized with CI.

text: Declare test/development-only dependencies in the project's shared dev/test dependency file rather than duplicating them in `tox.ini` `deps`; if a `tox.ini` factor-conditional dependency (`factor: package`) is used, ensure that factor also appears in `envlist` and the CI build matrix.
reason: Keeps dependency declarations authoritative and avoids dead tox configuration that is never evaluated, while ensuring all dev/test workflows can install the same dependency set.
scope: tox.ini deps / dev-test dependency files / CI matrix
common_pattern: Maintaining a consistent, valid, minimal tox/CI test matrix in tox.ini: envlist factor naming, basepython mappings, supported version combinations, dependency declarations, and keeping related config sections in sync.

text: Keep Wagtail Localize compatible with every supported Wagtail version documented in the README (currently 2.15, 4.1, 4.2): do not use newer-version-only APIs, template attributes, or icon names unconditionally; add a version-conditional fallback or legacy registration when older supported versions remain in the support matrix. Conversely, before removing version-gated code/markup or raising the minimum supported dependency/framework version, verify the actual minimum supported version. Remove now-unreachable version-compatibility branches, shims, flags, and markup attributes/classes/hooks that target an older version, replace them with direct calls to the supported API (running the project's `updatemodulepaths` tool where available), and document the reason for removal in the commit message; remove version-check compatibility shims once the minimum supported Wagtail version provides the native API. Keep any compatibility code or attributes still required by an older supported version and add an explanatory comment (e.g. 'needs to stay for Wagtail 4.1 compat') so future cleanups do not re-remove it. Do NOT remove version-gated code in historical migration files, since released migrations must continue to support upgrade paths from older framework versions.
reason: Dead compatibility code obscures the true supported-version floor and adds maintenance cost, but older still-supported Wagtail versions and released migrations must keep working. An explicit compatibility comment makes necessary legacy code discoverable to future maintainers.
common_pattern: Managing the lifecycle of dependency-version support: removing now-dead compatibility code when the minimum supported version is raised (while preserving historical migrations and documenting removals), and keeping the documented/declared support matrix aligned with what is actually tested and still maintained upstream.

text: Dependency version specifiers in packaging metadata (setup.py install_requires, pyproject.toml dependencies, tox.ini deps) must encode the actually supported/tested compatibility range: (a) set the lower bound to the true minimum supported version and bump it when dropping support (e.g. Django>=5.2), (b) omit unnecessary upper bounds when nightly/compat CI already exercises newer releases (prefer Wagtail>=4.1 over Wagtail>=4.1,<5.0), (c) when an upper bound is needed for testing against an upstream main branch, cap it at the next release line (vNext+1), (d) align bounds with upstream compatibility (don't cap below a version another dependency supports, e.g. Wagtail 6.2 supports Django 5.1), and (e) prefer the compatible-release operator ~=X.Y for test dependencies where a paired >=X.Y,<X.Z range is intended.
reason: Bounds that are looser or tighter than the real support matrix falsely advertise compatibility (or block compatible releases), causing downstream install conflicts and runtime breakage.
common_pattern: Dependency version constraints declared in packaging/config files (setup.py, pyproject.toml, tox.ini) should accurately encode the project's actually supported compatibility range: real lower bounds, upper bounds only when needed and aligned with the support matrix, with special handling for pre-releases and kept-in-sync support metadata.

text: When a dependency environment must install a release candidate or pre-release (e.g. in tox.ini), include the pre-release in the requirement specifier itself — use an exact pin like `pkg==x.yrc1` or a pre-release lower bound like `pkg>=x.y.rc1,<x.y+1`; do not rely on a stable range such as `>=x.y,<x.y+1`, which pip will resolve to the latest stable release instead of the RC.
reason: pip excludes pre-releases by default unless the specifier references a pre-release, so stable-style ranges silently fail to test the intended RC version.
common_pattern: Dependency version constraints declared in packaging/config files (setup.py, pyproject.toml, tox.ini) should accurately encode the project's actually supported compatibility range: real lower bounds, upper bounds only when needed and aligned with the support matrix, with special handling for pre-releases and kept-in-sync support metadata.

text: When adding or modifying model fields and migrations, check the existing model definition for equivalent fields, keep the code compatible with the project's minimum supported dependency versions (e.g., avoid Django 3.1+ only APIs while Django 2.11 is supported), and remove version-compatibility shims/kwargs constants by inlining modern required kwargs (e.g., use_json_field=True) once all supported versions accept them.
reason: This captures the shared principle of model-field hygiene across both PRs: avoid redundant fields, avoid incompatible newer APIs when older dependency versions are still supported, and eliminate dead compatibility code when the minimum supported version no longer requires it.
common_pattern: Model field definitions should be kept minimal and aligned with the project's supported dependency versions: avoid duplicate/existing fields, avoid newer-only APIs while older versions must be supported, and remove obsolete compatibility shims once minimum supported versions accept the modern API.

text: When adding a generated migration under a test app's `migrations/` directory, remove unnecessary `dependencies` entries — especially cross-app dependencies such as `wagtailcore` — unless the test models actually require them; these entries can cause test failures by coupling test database setup to application migration ordering.
reason: Generated migrations can over-declare dependencies, and unnecessary cross-app migration dependencies make tests depend on application migration history and ordering, which can break test database setup.
common_pattern: Generated migrations in test apps often over-declare migration dependencies, especially cross-app dependencies, and those unnecessary entries should be removed because they couple test database setup to application migration history and can cause test failures.

text: For optional Wagtail/Django app integrations, gate all integration points on app installation: only register views/URLs when the app is in INSTALLED_APPS; guard feature-specific Python branches with apps.is_installed("<app>") and import optional classes inline inside the guarded branch rather than at module scope; and for templates, build optional URL/config in a custom template tag that conditionally adds the integration entries instead of hardcoding {% url %} or loading the optional app at module level.
reason: Keeps optional integrations truly optional: projects can omit second-party packages without import failures, broken URL/view registration, hard dependencies, or template URL resolution errors.
common_pattern: Optional Wagtail/Django app integrations must be conditionally activated based on whether the app is installed, avoiding hard dependencies, top-level imports, and hardcoded template URLs.

text: Use domain-consistent, clearly distinguishing names for identifiers, variables, and model fields. Name variables and model fields after the exact model/type they reference (e.g., `snippet_revision` for a Snippet revision, `revision` for a FK to the generic `Revision` model, not `page_revision`). Avoid names that are easily confused with related concepts (e.g., `SegmentOverride` vs. `OverridableSegment`) or that replace an established domain term with a generic or newly introduced one. If a new term represents a genuine domain concept, define it and use it consistently across the module. For configurable translatable attributes, mirror the terminology used in the public docs (e.g., `translatable_fields`); do not invent block-specific variants such as `translatable_blocks` or `override_translatable_blocks`.
reason: Clear, domain-consistent terminology reduces cognitive load, prevents developers from using or modifying the wrong model/value, and keeps code aligned with documentation to avoid confusion and divergent override semantics. Misleadingly narrow names (e.g., `page_revision` for a `Revision` or Snippet revision) also cause readers to assume the wrong type.
common_pattern: Both generalizations concern naming and terminology quality: identifiers/model names should clearly reflect established domain concepts, distinguish distinct roles, and be used consistently across a module.

text: In `wagtail_localize/strings.py`, name validation functions after the full scope of what they validate (e.g., inline tag IDs, not just links). If validation broadens from link validation to all inline tags or attributes, rename the function accordingly.
reason: Function names should accurately describe their generalized behavior; keeping a link-specific name creates a misleading API for maintainers.
common_pattern: Inline-tag validation in wagtail_localize should reflect its actual scope: validation function names should match broadened responsibility, and validation should not reject inputs that the system already normalizes.

text: In `wagtail_localize/signals.py`, name signals with a `locale_` prefix (e.g., `locale_activated`) rather than `language_`, to match the `locale` argument they receive and the surrounding domain terminology.
reason: The signals pass a `locale` argument, so using `language_` creates inconsistent terminology and can confuse language vs. locale concepts.
common_pattern: Both generalizations converge on the same naming convention: signal names in `wagtail_localize/signals.py` should use `locale_` terminology to align with the `locale` argument, not `language_`.

text: In modules that import `gettext`/`gettext_lazy` as `_`, do not use bare `_` as a throwaway variable. Use a descriptive underscore-prefixed name such as `_created`, or restructure the code to avoid unpacking unused values.
reason: Bare `_` can shadow the translation function alias, causing confusing runtime errors, and it adds unused-variable noise.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail gettext/i18n conventions: avoid shadowing the `_` translation alias, choose `gettext_lazy` vs eager `gettext` based on evaluation/caching lifetime, and format translatable strings for translators.

text: Name boolean context/template flags consistently with the `has_` prefix (e.g., `has_legacy_styling`) and consolidate flags that represent the same condition into a single flag rather than exposing near-duplicates like `uses_legacy_header` and `has_editor_css`.
reason: Uniform boolean naming makes flags easier to recognize in context dictionaries and templates, while consolidation prevents redundant, divergent flags and gives templates one source of truth.
common_pattern: Managing boolean context/template flags as a single consistent set: use a uniform `has_` naming prefix and avoid exposing near-duplicate flags for the same underlying condition.

text: Use generic, version-agnostic directory names (e.g., `legacy/`) for code supporting older or deprecated versions rather than embedding version numbers in directory paths.
reason: Version-specific directory names become outdated and obscure the code's purpose; a generic `legacy/` label clearly indicates compatibility code and avoids renaming when versions change.
common_pattern: Managing the lifecycle of dependency-version support: removing now-dead compatibility code when the minimum supported version is raised (while preserving historical migrations and documenting removals), and keeping the documented/declared support matrix aligned with what is actually tested and still maintained upstream.

text: New Wagtail Localize Django settings must use the `WAGTAILLOCALIZE_` prefix (no underscore between `WAGTAIL` and `LOCALIZE`) and be named concisely for the behavior they control rather than using verbose object descriptions.
reason: Maintains a consistent settings namespace and makes setting names easier to read and remember.
common_pattern: Wagtail Localize Django settings should be named and designed around actual behavior: prefer mode/default selection over misleading disable flags, use the consistent WAGTAILLOCALIZE_ namespace with concise behavior-based names, and handle optional settings backward-compatibly with explicit branching.

text: Register custom Wagtail admin icons by adding an SVG under `templates/{package}/icons/` named after the full namespaced icon identifier (the SVG symbol `id` with the `icon-` prefix stripped, e.g. `wagtail-localize-convert.svg` for `icon-wagtail-localize-convert`), and reference it via `wagtail_hooks.py`. Prefer project-specific registered icons over generic built-in Wagtail icons when an action has clear domain semantics.
reason: Namespaced filenames avoid collisions across packages and make reused icons discoverable, while project-specific icons communicate domain actions more clearly and stay consistent with existing custom admin icons.
scope: package icon template files under `templates/{package}/icons/` and `wagtail_hooks.py`
common_pattern: Conventions for Wagtail admin icons in wagtail_localize: how custom icons are named, registered, selected, and passed to admin widgets.

text: For long compound boolean/conditional expressions, follow `black`'s formatting output, including line wrapping and splitting expressions across multiple lines (typically placing each logical clause on its own line and adding parentheses as needed). Do not manually reformat code to satisfy reviewer readability preferences; if a suggestion conflicts with `black`, keep the formatter-compliant form and explain that `black` determines layout.
reason: `black` is the project's single source of truth for formatting. Long boolean/conditional expressions should be wrapped consistently by `black`; manual reformatting will be reverted on the next `black` run and causes churn.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns are about improving readability of conditional logic: (a) line-wrapping long compound boolean expressions, and (b) consolidating redundant or overlapping conditional branches instead of duplicating structure.

text: Before defining a new UI action component under `common/components/`, check whether an identical or equivalent component already exists there; reuse it or extract a single generic action component (e.g. `ActionMenuButtonAction`) instead of creating per-location variants (e.g. `Header*Action`, `ActionMenu*Action`) that add no distinct behavior.
reason: Near-duplicate component definitions diverge over time, increase maintenance cost, and bloat the shared component API; consolidating keeps behavior consistent and the shared surface smaller.
common_pattern: Both generalizations address duplicate/near-duplicate UI action components in `common/components/` and advocate consolidation: either reusing an existing identical component or preferring a single generic action component over per-location variants.

text: When binding Django forms in views, prefer the shorthand `Form(request.POST or None)` over an `if request.method == 'POST'` branch — `None` yields an unbound form and non-POST requests fall through naturally. However, if an empty POST submission must still bind the form and run validation (e.g., required fields like no locales selected should raise errors), use an explicit `if request.method == 'POST'` check instead, since `request.POST or None` treats an empty QueryDict as no submission and leaves the form unbound.
reason: The shorthand is simpler and equivalent in the common case, but silently skips validation on empty POSTs, which breaks required-field validation and tests expecting errors.
common_pattern: Django form binding idiom: the `request.POST or None` shorthand vs. explicit `request.method == 'POST'` check, and when the shorthand's equivalence to the if/else breaks (empty POST must still bind and validate).

text: When the same declaration or initialization is repeated across multiple branches (e.g., switch cases or if/else blocks), hoist it to a single shared definition before the branching logic instead of re-declaring it per branch.
reason: Avoids duplicated setup, prevents unnecessary re-creation of values or components on each branch, and creates a single source of truth for the shared definition.
common_pattern: Hoisting duplicated declarations or initializations out of branching constructs (switch cases, conditional branches) into a single shared definition before the branches.

text: Consolidate overlapping conditional branches instead of duplicating them: merge a new check that repeats an existing condition in the same scope into the existing branch, express mutually exclusive adjacent paths as if/else rather than sequential ifs, and fold elif branches that share a type check into a single elif with a nested secondary condition.
reason: Reduces duplicated conditions, makes mutual exclusivity explicit, and keeps related behavior co-located so branches don't diverge or accidentally execute together during future changes.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns are about improving readability of conditional logic: (a) line-wrapping long compound boolean expressions, and (b) consolidating redundant or overlapping conditional branches instead of duplicating structure.

text: When deriving HTML `id` values (and same-page `href="#..."` fragments) from arbitrary labels or user-facing text, sanitize the label into a valid ID (e.g. slugify/normalize) and reuse that exact same sanitized ID everywhere it is referenced, such as `aria-controls`, `href`, and any associated JS lookups — do not merely lowercase the raw text.
reason: Raw labels can contain spaces or special characters; unsanitized IDs become invalid, break ARIA relationships, and produce fragment links that fail to resolve.
common_pattern: All four generalizations concern handling HTML `id` attributes: (a) generating valid, reusable IDs from arbitrary labels, and (b) extracting/validating IDs without assuming they only appear on `<a>` tags. They share the same subject matter (HTML id attribute management) but split into two distinct sub-patterns: ID *creation/sanitization* versus ID *extraction/validation scope and messaging*.

text: In export/serialization code that feeds ordered output (e.g., `export_po` message entries), use an order-preserving collection (list or dict) instead of `set()`, since set iteration order is not guaranteed and would make generated output nondeterministic.
reason: Sets do not preserve insertion order, which makes exported output nondeterministic, produces noisy diffs, and can break tests or consumers that rely on the ordering of exported entries.
common_pattern: All three generalizations state the same principle in varying abstraction levels: collections that feed order-sensitive output (specifically the PO export path) must use order-preserving structures (list/dict) rather than `set`, because set iteration order is not guaranteed.

text: In Wagtail frontend/admin JavaScript, when supporting IE11, avoid NodeList.prototype.forEach and other unsupported ES6+ browser APIs; use a compatible construct such as a `for` loop over `querySelectorAll` results or include an appropriate polyfill.
reason: IE11 does not implement NodeList.prototype.forEach, so using it in inline admin template JavaScript causes runtime errors and breaks the UI.
common_pattern: Browser compatibility in frontend JavaScript: avoid APIs unsupported by targeted browsers (notably IE11), such as NodeList.prototype.forEach, and use compatible constructs or a polyfill instead.

text: Use the dictionary iteration or conversion method that directly matches your intent: use `.values()` when only values are needed instead of `.items()` with an unused key, and use `list(mapping.items())` directly when the desired result is the list of key-value pairs rather than rebuilding them via a comprehension.
reason: This keeps iteration focused, avoids unused variables and redundant tuple construction, and makes the code simpler and more efficient.
common_pattern: Avoid unnecessary or redundant use of `dict.items()`: choose the dictionary API that directly matches what the code needs, and avoid unpacking/rebuilding key-value pairs when no transformation is required.

text: In wagtail_localize segment ingestion, synchronise all translatable fields before processing segments by using the shared field predicate in wagtail_localize/fields.py; if the predicate excludes fields needed for this operation, broaden the predicate centrally rather than special-casing field types at call sites.
reason: Keeps segment ingestion consistent across field types, avoids acting on stale or unsynchronised field data, and prevents divergent field-classification logic.
common_pattern: Centralize segment-ingestion field synchronization through the shared field predicate, broadening that predicate when necessary instead of special-casing field types at call sites.

text: When a value may be absent, use the built-in lookup-with-default form instead of checking presence and then falling back — read optional dict entries with `self.options.get(key, default)` rather than `if key in self.options: ...`, and read optional attributes with `getattr(obj, 'attr', default)` rather than `hasattr(obj, 'attr')` plus a conditional. Prefer the default-argument form as it expresses the fallback in one place, avoids a duplicate lookup, and matches existing precedent in the codebase.
reason: The with-default APIs are more concise and idiomatic, avoid a separate membership/attribute existence check and the resulting double lookup, and clearly state the fallback value in a single expression.
common_pattern: Both generalizations recommend replacing a presence check plus fallback assignment (membership test on a dict, or hasattr on an object) with the idiomatic single-call lookup-with-default API (dict.get / getattr), which is more concise, avoids duplicate lookup, and makes the default explicit.

text: In translatable strings, prefer named placeholders such as `%(name)s` with a dict mapping instead of positional placeholders such as `%s`.
reason: Named placeholders give translators clearer context and match the established Wagtail core and localize convention.
common_pattern: Django/Wagtail gettext/i18n conventions: avoid shadowing the `_` translation alias, choose `gettext_lazy` vs eager `gettext` based on evaluation/caching lifetime, and format translatable strings for translators.

text: Extract complex or deeply nested conditional branches (such as multi-way URL resolution logic) into dedicated helper functions rather than leaving them inline; when analogous sibling logic exists, extract it in the same way for consistency.
reason: Reduces visual complexity and makes control flow easier to read and maintain, while keeping parallel code paths consistently structured.
common_pattern: Extract complex nested inline conditionals into dedicated helper functions, and apply the same extraction to parallel sibling logic for consistency.

text: Inline comments that describe an action performed by the code should use the imperative present tense (e.g., 'Remove ...' rather than 'Removed ...').
reason: Imperative present tense matches conventional code comment grammar and keeps comments consistent across the codebase.
common_pattern: Guidelines for writing inline comments: explain non-obvious rationale and use imperative present tense.

text: When aligning a UI component with the shared design system (e.g., Wagtail 4.0), remove obsolete or ad-hoc decorative indicators such as arrows in colored label/badge boxes rather than adjusting their dimensions, colors, or restyling them in place.
reason: Prevents outdated visual affordances from persisting and keeps the interface consistent with the shared design language.
common_pattern: Aligning UI components with the shared design system by removing obsolete or ad-hoc decorative indicators (e.g., arrows in colored label/badge boxes) instead of restyling or resizing them.

text: In nested SCSS, ensure every `&--modifier` block is closed before the next sibling `&--modifier` block begins; when reformatting or removing blank lines, verify brace balance so that adjacent modifiers remain siblings and do not become nested (which would compile to incorrect chained class names like `.icon--green--red` instead of `.icon--red`).
reason: Blank-line cleanup and other formatting edits can accidentally remove structural closing braces, silently changing the compiled CSS output and breaking modifier styling.
common_pattern: Preventing accidental nesting of sibling SCSS modifier blocks due to missing closing braces when editing or reformatting nested SCSS.

text: Use `zip(..., strict=True)` for project lint compliance (ruff B905); when strictness causes tests with mocked data to fail, update mock responses so all zipped iterables have matching lengths instead of suppressing or weakening the strict check.
reason: Avoids silent truncation from mismatched iterables, keeps code compliant with project lint rules, and ensures mocked test data reflects real response structure rather than giving false confidence.
common_pattern: Strict zip semantics: use `zip(strict=True)` for lint compliance, and ensure test mocks preserve matching iterable lengths rather than bypassing the strict check.

text: Run the project's pre-commit hooks locally (e.g. `pre-commit install && pre-commit run --all-files`) before submitting changes, including documentation-only edits, to catch lint and formatting issues before CI or review.
reason: Catches lint/format problems early, reduces CI failures and review churn, and applies to docs changes as well as code.
common_pattern: Managing linting/formatting tooling through pre-commit as the single source of truth — centralizing dependency versions there, running hooks locally before submission, and keeping hook revisions current and synchronized with CI.

text: Keep optional sub-app-specific code and assets inside that sub-app's own package rather than in shared/core modules or top-level directories. This includes views/templates (e.g., `wagtail_localize/modeladmin/views.py` and `wagtail_localize/modeladmin/templates/...`) and management commands (e.g., `wagtail_localize/translation/management/commands/` instead of top-level `wagtail_localize/management/commands/`).
reason: Optional sub-apps may not always be installed or enabled; isolating their code preserves the optional boundary, prevents core modules from depending on optional sub-app code, and ensures disabling a sub-app also disables its views, templates, and commands.
common_pattern: Management commands that implement optional sub-app functionality must be placed under the sub-app's own `management/commands/` directory (e.g. `<app>/<sub_app>/management/commands/`) rather than the top-level app's `management/commands/`, so that disabling the optional sub-app also disables its commands.

text: When yielding Wagtail admin button widgets from hooks, pass `icon_name` directly to the `wagtailadmin_widgets.Button(...)` constructor instead of constructing the button and then assigning `button.icon_name` via a helper.
reason: Wagtail's `Button` widget supports `icon_name` natively, so direct constructor use is simpler, avoids unnecessary compatibility wrappers, and keeps hook definitions closer to the upstream API.
common_pattern: Conventions for Wagtail admin icons in wagtail_localize: how custom icons are named, registered, selected, and passed to admin widgets.

text: Before merging, remove stale artifacts from source: TODO/FIXME comments whose work is already implemented or tracked outside the codebase, and commented-out code. If a block is only invalid under a specific dependency version, guard it with an explicit version check (e.g., `if WAGTAIL_VERSION >= (4, 0, 0):`) instead of commenting it out; otherwise delete it. Version control history already preserves removed code.
reason: Leftover TODO markers and commented-out code indicate unfinished or abandoned work, add noise, become stale or forgotten, and make intent unclear. An explicit version guard documents dependency compatibility better than a comment.
common_pattern: Removing stale, non-functional artifacts (TODO/FIXME comments and commented-out code) from source before merge, with an explicit version-guard alternative when conditionally-valid code would otherwise be commented out.

text: Write documentation and UI help text so wording matches the actual effect of a setting or capability: describe what a setting changes (e.g., 'Configure the default X') rather than overstating it as 'disabling X' when the feature remains available, and prefer plain descriptive phrases (e.g., 'models that support drafts') over ad-hoc compound adjectives (e.g., 'draft-able models'). In wagtail_localize, help text for publish/update and translation-sync actions must also accurately describe actual behavior and edge cases — e.g., changes remaining in the original language until translated, and sources that have never been published — rather than using unconditional or inconsistent wording.
reason: Accurate, plain wording prevents users from believing a feature is turned off entirely or from being confused by ambiguous jargon about what qualifies. In localization workflows, help text must reflect the actual untranslated state and never-published edge cases of publish/update and translation-sync actions.
scope: docs and UI help text, including wagtail_localize publish/update/translation-sync help text
common_pattern: Help text for localization publish/translation actions must accurately describe actual behavior, defaults, and edge cases instead of making unconditional or misleading claims.

text: When writing conditional UI help text for related publish/action options, use a sentence structure consistent with the related help messages and refer to other options by their exact UI label (e.g., "Use machine translation").
reason: Inconsistent wording and paraphrased option names between related help messages confuse users and make option interactions harder to understand.
scope: wagtail_localize UI help text / view-level constants
common_pattern: User-facing documentation and help text should use wording that accurately describes the actual behavior of a feature and stays plain and consistent with related text, rather than labels that overstate effects or use ad-hoc jargon.

text: When a class or module wraps or integrates a third-party/external API (e.g., machine translator integrations in `wagtail_localize/machine_translators/`), include a link to that API's official documentation in the class or module docstring.
reason: Keeps integration context close to the code and saves future developers from independently searching for the external API's source of truth.
common_pattern: Wrapping or integrating an external/third-party API should be documented with a link to that API's official reference in the wrapper's class or module docstring.

text: In integration how-to docs (e.g. `docs/how-to/integrations/*.md`), use inline comments inside example configuration code blocks to annotate values: mark placeholders users must customize (endpoints, URLs, keys), explain when a value is optional or behaves differently for self-hosted instances (and what to use there), and embed a link to the upstream provider's official API reference next to provider-specific options instead of as a separate markdown link after the code block.
reason: Keeps explanatory context co-located with the option it describes, removes ambiguity about whether a shown value is the only valid choice, and aligns docs with the provider's authoritative source of truth.
common_pattern: In provider-integration how-to docs, inline comments inside example configuration code blocks should carry explanatory context — annotating values users are expected to customize/override (and how they differ for self-hosted setups) and linking to the upstream provider's API reference for provider-specific options.

text: In `wagtail_localize/models.py`, docstrings for translation import/export methods must accurately state the direction (importing vs exporting) and what data is included (e.g., 'Imports all translatable strings with any translations that have already been made.').
reason: Callers of translation import/export workflows rely on correct docstrings to know whether strings are being read in or written out and what gets included.
common_pattern: Both sub-groups concern Wagtail localization translation import/export correctness, but they address different concerns: (a) docstrings accurately describing import/export direction and content, and (b) the PO import command not fabricating translations by substituting source text for empty msgstr.

text: When rewriting a README, preserve existing links such as badges, docs references, and related project links instead of dropping them; only remove links intentionally.
reason: Links provide navigation, project status, and reference information; losing them reduces the usefulness of the README.
common_pattern: README presentation conventions: preserving navigational links and using visually prominent badge styles for primary call-to-action links.

text: In README badge rows, use the Shields.io `style=for-the-badge` style for the primary Documentation call-to-action badge to make it visually prominent.
reason: A prominent documentation badge makes the docs link stand out from secondary metadata badges such as version, license, coverage, and language grade.
scope: README badge formatting, especially primary documentation links
common_pattern: README presentation conventions: preserving navigational links and using visually prominent badge styles for primary call-to-action links.

text: Use the official/canonical capitalization for product and proper nouns (e.g., `Google Cloud`, `Wagtail`, `Python`, `JavaScript`) in documentation and changelog entries, matching the casing used elsewhere in the same file and in the vendor's official brand/naming. Reserve lowercase forms for code identifiers, import paths, package names, and repository slugs.
reason: Changelog entries and docs are user-facing; consistent canonical capitalization improves polish, avoids confusion, and keeps search results and naming uniform across the project.
common_pattern: All generalizations state the same principle: user-facing documentation and changelog prose must use the official/canonical capitalization of product and proper nouns (e.g., `Google Cloud`, `Wagtail`, `Python`, `JavaScript`), reserving lowercase only for code identifiers, slugs, and import paths. The Wagtail-specific entries (Gens 2–4, 6) are entity-specific instances of the broader rule already stated in Gens 1 and 5.

text: Inline comments should explain non-obvious design decisions (especially when a destructive operation has a plausible less-destructive alternative) rather than merely restating what the code does.
reason: Future maintainers need the intent behind surprising or destructive behavior to avoid accidental changes or misunderstandings.
common_pattern: Guidelines for writing inline comments: explain non-obvious rationale and use imperative present tense.

text: In MkDocs Material documentation, render notes, caveats, and supplementary setup requirements as admonition blocks (e.g. `!!! note`, `!!! attention`) with indented content instead of ad-hoc bold/italic notes or plain paragraphs; inside an admonition, state the note directly without redundant lead-ins such as 'Note that'.
reason: Admonitions are the supported MkDocs Material syntax, render consistently and semantically across the documentation site, and already signal note scope, so repeating that scope in prose is redundant.
common_pattern: MkDocs Material documentation formatting convention: use admonition blocks for notes/caveats and write them concisely without redundant lead-ins.

text: In README installation/setup instructions, document any Django management command that the package's features require (for example `collectstatic` when the package adds static assets): use the minimal default invocation without optional flags (omit `--link` and similar), and add a short note explaining what the command does and why it is needed, without duplicating generic Django deployment documentation.
reason: New users may spend significant time debugging missing assets or misconfigured setup because a required step isn't documented; showing the simplest working command avoids implying optional flags are required, while a brief explanation clarifies why the generic Django step applies to this package's specific features.
common_pattern: Documenting Django management commands (e.g. `collectstatic`) in a package's README setup instructions: use the minimal default invocation and briefly explain why the command is needed for the package's features, rather than presenting optional flags as required or omitting the step entirely.

text: When documenting an allowlist/opt-in parameter that excludes nested block fields from translation, warn users that overrideable segments (e.g. images) may lose their default per-locale override behavior, and explain how to preserve it by adding those fields to the allowlist.
reason: Without this warning, users may unintentionally lose Wagtail's default ability to override media or other segments per locale.
common_pattern: Both sub-patterns concern how a translation feature should surface its configuration to users: (a) naming configurable attributes consistently with public documented terminology, and (b) documenting the side effects of allowlist-style exclusion parameters. Gen 1 and Gen 2 converge tightly on attribute naming; Gen 3 is a distinct documentation concern from the same feature.

text: In CHANGELOG.md, place each entry under the Keep a Changelog section that matches the nature of the change: use `### Changed` for compatibility/workflow/test-matrix updates and other non-bug modifications, reserve `### Fixed` for actual bug fixes, and reserve `### Removed` for user-facing removals. When a change both adds and removes comparable items (e.g. test-matrix versions), record it as a single `### Changed` entry rather than separate `### Added`/`### Removed` entries.
reason: Correct section placement keeps the changelog semantically accurate; a compatibility update made only by editing the test matrix is a change, not a fix.
common_pattern: CHANGELOG.md authoring conventions — entries must be semantically categorized, consolidated rather than fragmented, and written in a consistent human-authored voice/style.

text: How-to documentation that describes a concrete scenario should include a code snippet showing the relevant setup and usage (e.g., in docs/how-to/tips.md, scenario-based tips should include an illustrative snippet) so readers can contextualize the scenario.
reason: Concrete examples make abstract documentation scenarios understandable and help readers map the described situation to their own code.
scope: docs/how-to guides, especially scenario-based tips in docs/how-to/tips.md
common_pattern: Scenario-based how-to documentation should include concrete code snippets to make abstract guidance understandable.

text: Proofread comments and user-facing documentation (including tutorial markdown) before committing or submitting; remove typos, stray/leading characters, misspellings, and unfinished fragments, correcting them via suggested edits—especially in prose that users will copy and follow verbatim.
reason: Careless editing (typos, stray characters, leftover fragments) reduces readability, clarity, credibility, and professionalism, and can mislead readers of code explanations or step-by-step instructions.
common_pattern: All three generalizations call for proofreading documentation prose to correct spelling and typos before submission, emphasizing user-facing markdown clarity and professionalism.

text: Code examples and identifiers in documentation must be exact and copy-pasteable: use correctly spelled package/module/class names, valid importable paths from the documented library itself (not paths from demo or third-party projects such as `bakerydemo.*`), and real setting/parameter names — never rely on the reader to infer or fix the correct identifier.
reason: Readers follow documentation literally; misspelled identifiers (`wagtaiil_localize`), wrong setting names (`LANGAUGE_CODE`), invalid imports, or demo-project paths break their projects at runtime, fail documentation linting, and undermine the docs as a source of truth.
common_pattern: Code identifiers appearing in documentation (imports, module paths, setting names, class/function/parameter names) must be both exact/copy-pasteable and consistently formatted as inline code in prose.

text: In documentation prose, format code identifiers (class names, function names, parameter names, module paths, setting names) as inline code using backticks, consistent with the surrounding document; do not additionally wrap inline code spans in bold markup.
reason: Inline-code formatting visually distinguishes identifiers from prose and matches the project's existing documentation conventions, while bold around inline code is redundant and makes rendering inconsistent.
common_pattern: Code identifiers appearing in documentation (imports, module paths, setting names, class/function/parameter names) must be both exact/copy-pasteable and consistently formatted as inline code in prose.

text: Keep all published support metadata synchronized with the actual dependency support matrix. This includes: (1) removing classifiers (e.g., in setup.py) for versions the project no longer supports; (2) adding a comment or link to upstream compatibility documentation when pinning a dependency for a specific compatibility reason; (3) keeping documented supported-versions lists (e.g., README.md) in sync with the versions actually built/tested in CI and with upstream end-of-life data (e.g., endoflife.date) — remove end-of-life/untested versions and add only currently supported ones rather than listing both the outgoing and incoming versions or accumulating historical versions; and (4) when a PR drops support or testing for a version, recording it in CHANGELOG.md under the `### Removed` section (e.g., `- Drop {tool} testing for {dependency/version}`).
reason: Stale classifiers, undocumented pins, and unsupported or untested version lists misrepresent the project's supported versions to users, package indexes, and future maintainers, lose the rationale for pinning decisions, and mislead users into assuming support that no longer receives security fixes, while omitting newly supported versions hides available compatibility.
common_pattern: Managing the lifecycle of dependency-version support: removing now-dead compatibility code when the minimum supported version is raised (while preserving historical migrations and documenting removals), and keeping the documented/declared support matrix aligned with what is actually tested and still maintained upstream.

text: Consolidate related CHANGELOG.md entries — especially those sharing the same PR reference or describing the net effect of one change — into a single concise bullet rather than listing every individual change or commit separately.
reason: Merged entries are easier to read and avoid fragmented, low-value bullet lists that mirror commits instead of describing user-facing changes.
common_pattern: CHANGELOG.md authoring conventions — entries must be semantically categorized, consolidated rather than fragmented, and written in a consistent human-authored voice/style.

text: Write CHANGELOG.md entries in a natural, human-authored voice matching the style used across the project's other repositories, using consistent verb tense/phrasing and consistent capitalization for the same term across adjacent related entries (e.g. all 'Add ...' or all 'Remove ...').
reason: Consistent, human-written changelogs are more readable and maintain a uniform tone; mixed casing or phrasing of the same subject term looks sloppy.
common_pattern: CHANGELOG.md authoring conventions — entries must be semantically categorized, consolidated rather than fragmented, and written in a consistent human-authored voice/style.
